risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: api/_lib/compliance-rules.js evaluateTraining()'s optional per-staff branch answered meets:TRUE for a staff member with ZERO recorded training hours, in a state that mandates them. Driven 2026-09-26 against the real committed seed: West Virginia, staff member with annual_hours_recorded 0, returned { required_annual_hours: 0, recorded_annual_hours: 0, shortfall_hours: 0, meets: TRUE, applicable_requirements: [null, null] }. WV mandates 8 hours a year for an administrator and 2 hours a year of dementia training for ALL staff under 64 CSR 14. Its requirement rows are shaped {audience, hours_per_year, topic}; this branch reads r.who and r.annual_hours, so every requirement contributed Number(undefined) || 0 and the applicable_requirements array came back as [null, null]. A DIFFERENT VOCABULARY WAS READ AS AN EMPTY ONE, and once summed an empty requirement set is indistinguishable from a satisfied one. A SECOND FABRICATION SURVIVES A CORRECT VOCABULARY AND IS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: Pennsylvania rows carry additive:true, a secured-dementia-unit requirement ON TOP OF the general annual hours, so collapsing 12 general and 6 dementia into one target of 18 and comparing one recorded total meant a staff member with 18 hours of general training and no dementia training read as compliant -- UNDER-requires, a false PASS; and Ohio rows carry counts_toward_general_annual:true, 4 and 8 hours that count TOWARD the general 8 rather than adding to it, so summing all four rows produced a required total of 29 where the code requires less -- OVER-requires, a false FAIL, which is the merciful direction and is still a wrong number on a compliance board. Both fields are machine-readable and present on the real seeded rows; nothing was reading either. THE BRANCH HAS NEVER FIRED: sairncare.html's cqShowTraining() sends {state, facility_class, requirement_type} and no staff array, so the whole branch is dormant and none of this has reached a screen -- which is the only reason this is a latent defect rather than an incident, and is not a reason to leave it, because the open request that surfaced it was to BUILD the caller. FIXED BY REFUSING RATHER THAN GUESSING, matching this module's own stated standard that nothing is ever silently substituted: a requirement row carrying neither `who` nor `annual_hours` now returns REQUIREMENTS_NOT_JOINABLE naming the state, the rule and the unreadable rows' key sets; and any applicable requirement carrying stacking semantics (additive, counts_toward_general_annual, or an explicit stacking field) now yields meets:null with a meets_unknown_reason rather than a boolean in either direction, while still reporting the recorded and required figures. Measured across all six seeded training rules after the fix: OH null, IN false, MI not applicable, PA/alr null, PA/pch null, WV refused -- one of six states can currently be answered at all.

risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: sairnsenior.html rfDeliveredHoursFor(clientId) read `v.actual_start` and `v.actual_end`. A sen_visits row has no such fields -- the clock is `clock_in_at` / `clock_out_at`, which the authorisation burn-down (~:2540), the visit card (~:2964) and visitHours() (~:3925) all read correctly. So the guard `if(!v.actual_start||!v.actual_end)return;` was true for every visit ever recorded, the loop added nothing, and THE FUNCTION RETURNED 0 FOR EVERY CLIENT FOR AS LONG AS IT EXISTED. rfPerformance() hands that to the Referral Sources table. THE ZERO WAS WORSE THAN A BLANK because the renderer already distinguishes them: `p.linked ? p.hours.toFixed(1)+' h' : '--'`. An unlinked source correctly showed '--' meaning we cannot attribute hours; a LINKED source showed a confident '0.0 h', which reads as "we looked, and this source's clients received no care" -- against real clocked visits. Guardian's fabricated-KPI check could not see it: the figure is backed by a real function doing real arithmetic over a real array, and the fabrication arrives through a field NAME. The function's own comment was already the specification -- "Reuses the same only-count-what-was-actually-clocked rule the authorisation burn-down uses" -- and was true of the intent and false of the field names. Fixed by CALLING visitHours() rather than carrying a third copy of the clock arithmetic, which is what that function's own header asks for ("so both compute delivered hours the same way -- a claim and an insufficient-hours finding must never silently diverge on this arithmetic"). Reachability checked rather than assumed: both are inside the script block spanning ~1339-6052. 11 arms in tests/sairnsenior_referral_hours.js, driven in a vm sandbox against visit fixtures rather than grepped.

risks.risk: api/sd-data.js alf_billing derive_charges: the reconciliation read `invRows[0].data.charge_lines` as the prior invoice's line detail. NO WRITE PATH ON THIS PLATFORM STORES THAT KEY -- sairncare.html's invoice record carries id, month, room_board_amount, care_amount, private_total, private_status, hcbs_claim_amount, hcbs_status, care_level_breakdown, revision_history and generated_by, and no per-event lines at all. So priorLines was ALWAYS [], and careCharges.reconcileAgainstInvoice(derived, []) answers: every derived line ADDED, nothing removed, nothing changed, unchanged_count 0, and net_change equal to the ENTIRE derived amount -- returned beside `invoice_exists: true`, which is what made the figure read as a comparison rather than as a first look. On the view this branch's own comment calls "the audit trail that replaces the manual reconciliation". THE ARGUMENT FOR THE FIX WAS ALREADY WRITTEN TWELVE LINES ABOVE IT, for the adjacent case: the 2026-09-04 hardening of the UNREADABLE prior invoice says "this fell back to [], so the reconciliation reported EVERY derived line as new ... Somebody regenerates on the strength of that." The read below it then did exactly that for an invoice that was read perfectly well. Fixed as a named third state -- reconciliation_vs_invoice null, reconciliation_unavailable PRIOR_INVOICE_HAS_NO_CHARGE_LINES, and a sentence saying comparing against nothing would report every charge as new and the net change as the whole invoice. AND THE CLIENT HALF TOO: sairncare.html's renderer guards on `invoice_exists && rv`, so a bare null would have replaced a wrong figure with SILENCE and left the same person deciding with no more information than before; it now renders the reason. NO PRIOR INVOICE is deliberately left alone -- with nothing on file every derived line genuinely is new and invoice_exists:false says so.

risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: tools/ghost_field_read_scan.py built its spelled-field universe from RAW file text including comments, with *.md in the source list. The tool's rule is that a gate reading a field never spelled anywhere cannot be true -- so ANY PROSE MENTIONING A DEAD FIELD NAME MAKES IT "SPELLED" AND SILENCES THE DETECTOR FOR IT PERMANENTLY. Demonstrated by the fix committed in the same change: writing the regression arm "rfDeliveredHoursFor must not read actual_start" put the words actual_start in a comment, and the scan stopped reporting actual_start. Writing the test for a dead field disabled the standing detector for that field. This is PR 1.11's sibling in the other direction and PR 1.1 exactly -- a check that stopped checking -- committed inside a tool whose entire subject is a condition that cannot fire, by the author of the sweep document that named the class. CAUGHT BY THE CONTROL, NOT BY REVIEW: tests/run_ghost_field_read_probe.py MUTATION 1 restores the real shipped pre-fix rfDeliveredHoursFor body into the real sairnsenior.html and demands the scan NAME actual_start; it exited 1 FINDING (so a count-only arm would have passed) and did not name the field. Fixed: spellings now come from code and data and never from prose -- comments stripped from .js/.html/.cjs/.mjs and from .py with a quote-aware # scanner, strings KEPT because a string key is a real spelling, and .md excluded outright. The cost is stated in the tool header rather than left to be found: a field defined ONLY in a markdown spec now reads as a ghost, which is the false-positive direction a human dismisses in one read.

risks.basis: the same app (sairnsenior) has this defect on record
risks.risk: A caregiver whose CPR certification had expired could be assigned to a client and scheduled onto a visit, on all three write paths -- saveClient(), senReassignClient() and saveVisit() -- while the app already held the expiry date, already computed the days remaining with certDaysUntil(), and already rendered a red "Expired" badge for that same caregiver on the Caregivers panel. Two screens gave two answers about the same person and nothing flagged the disagreement. The underlying reason no check existed is structural rather than an omission: assigned_employee_id is an employee_id from SAIRNbiz's roster and a sen_caregivers row is keyed CG-... with a name, so there was no field joining the assignment to the certificate. Fixed by declaring the link (a "Linked employee" select on the caregiver record) and gating all three paths through it before any write; an expired certificate refuses and names the date and the day count, while an unlinked or undated record is a third state that allows and says so rather than passing silently.

risks.basis: the same app (sairnsenior) has this defect on record
risks.risk: sen_visits clock_flags were ASSIGNED, not merged. api/sd-data.js's EVV branch did visitData.clock_flags = clockCheck.flags, and a visit's two halves arrive as TWO separate writes -- checkClockEvent only reports on the clock fields present in THIS payload, so the clock-out's write REPLACED the clock-in's flags and a LATE_REPLAY on the way in vanished with nothing saying it had existed. The per-field SKEW STAMPS do not have the problem because they are KEYED; this was the one unkeyed array. Found in cody's b8 Tier A review of hank's api/ work, not by any checker. It only shows when BOTH halves are flagged, which is the case a state EVV audit asks about -- with a clean clock-out the array is empty, the guard never fires, and the first flag survives by luck. Fixed by merging on field, with the superseded set taken from the PAYLOAD rather than from the new flags: a field this payload re-reported has been re-checked so its stale flag must go EVEN IF the re-check produced none, and a field it did not mention was not checked so its flag is kept. The key stays ABSENT when there is nothing to say, because api/sd-data-sen-evv-clock.test.js:200 asserts that on a clean write. CLOCK_FIELDS hoisted out of api/_lib/sen-evv-clock.js and exported rather than re-listed.
